sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Legal pages and attribution checks
sections.what: Checks the required statements on the terms, privacy and AI pages, checks each rights policy has its credit on the attributions page, and checks the legal footer links appear on the roster page.
sections.why: Keeps required legal content present and in step with the data-source policies.
sections.watch_out: Exact-phrase checks will fail on any edit to legal wording, so changes need to update the test together.

summary: Browser tests that check the terms, privacy, AI and attribution pages say what they must, and that every rights policy file gets its own attribution entry and every app page has the legal footer links.
purpose: Confirms the required legal and trust content is present and generated from the rights data.
why: Legal pages must contain specific promises such as the 18-plus rule and the no-money statement, and third-party credits must be listed.
how: It opens the terms page and checks its heading and key sentences, then the privacy page for required section names, then the AI page for the labelling and verifier statements. The attribution test reads every JSON file in the rights policies folder and checks each display name and attribution text appears on the attributions page. The footer test checks the roster page shows the four legal links.
inputs: The legal pages and the rights policy JSON files.
outputs: Pass or fail for each required phrase, attribution entry and footer link.
risks: The attribution test depends on the file path being relative to the project root. Any wording change to legal pages will break the exact phrase checks.
debug: Check the failing phrase on the page and compare it with the expected wording. For attribution failures, confirm the policy file's display name and text match the page.
